narr: An outflow boundary from early morning storms extended south from Eastern Oklahoma into East Texas by the afternoon hours on May 13th, while an upper low pressure area remained stationary near the South Texas coast. Strong daytime heating within a moist air mass in place contributed to moderate instability that developed during the afternoon, with widely scattered showers and thunderstorms igniting near and east of the outflow boundary across portions of East Texas and North Louisiana. An isolated severe thunderstorm developed near Hughes Springs in Cass County, downing trees near the roadway. Another isolated thunderstorm produced very heavy rainfall in a short period of time just south of Mount Pleasant, resulting in flash flooding which stalled a vehicle in the high water. These storms diminished during the evening with the loss of heating and instability.
ev: High water was reported south of I-30 near Highway 271 near Mount Pleasant. One car was stalled in the flood waters.
lsr: FLOODING REPORTED SOUTH OF I-30 NEAR US HIGHWAY 271. ONE CAR WAS STALLED BY FLOOD WATERS.
